sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The Mitteler Rebbe explains the distinction between the nullification of speech to thought and the nullification of thought to intellect, using the analogy of a rider and chariot.

translations.translation: And the Mitteler Rebbe explains this in Shaarei Teshuvah,
by prefacing the distinction between the nullification of speech to thought and the nullification of thought to intellect.
For the nullification of speech to thought is not a complete nullification.
For although in order for speech to be ordered, it is through speech receiving from thought,
in addition to the fact that before speaking one must arrange in his thought how to speak
[as is known
regarding the matter of saying it four times to himself],
nevertheless, even during the actual speech, thought must illuminate within the speech so that it be according to the instruction of thought,
nevertheless,
speech in its essential essence is separate from thought,
and its nullification to thought is only regarding that the order of the letters of speech be according to the instruction of thought.
And it is like the nullification of the chariot to the rider, where the chariot is an independent entity and the nullification of the horses
(chariot)
to the rider is only regarding that their movement be according to the will of the rider.
However, the nullification of the letters of thought to the intellect is
(not only regarding the order of the letters, but also)
in their essential existence,
for in order for there to be letters of thought, it is specifically through the intellect
(or the emotions)
that is clothed within them
[And that thought is always roaming is because the intellect and emotions are always felt in man].
And furthermore,
the very essence of the letters of thought is that they receive from the intellect or emotions that are clothed within them.
And the explanation is,
that the distinction between thought and speech is also in the manner of their connection to the intellect and emotions that are clothed within them.
For thought is a unified garment and speech is a separate garment.
For the essence of speech is that a person clothes his intellect and emotions in an entity
(letters)
that is outside of himself,
therefore,
although in order for speech to exist
(from the perspective of the speaker)
it is specifically when speech receives from his intellect and emotions,
nevertheless,
after speech already exists,
it is heard also by another and is separate from the speaker.
And the essence of the letters of thought is that the intellect and emotions of the thinker are revealed through them,
and therefore,
even after the letters of thought exist,
they do not go out outside of him.
Now, in the nullification of the letters of thought to the intellect, there are two general levels.
When one thinks the intellect in its letters
[and certainly when one thinks how to influence the intellect to another,
and as above, before speech one must arrange in his thought how to speak],
for in this thought,
the letters are felt,
except that they are unified with the intellect,
as above.
And when one thinks the intellect itself
[thought within thought],
in this thought the letters are not felt,
for they are included and nullified within the intellect.
And this is what the tribes said to Yaakov: "There is nothing but One in your heart"
(specifically "in your heart"),
for the meaning of "nothing but One" is that there is no existence besides Him,
not even an existence that is nullified to Him.
And therefore they said "there is nothing but One in your heart"
(even though the Patriarchs are themselves the Chariot, and the nullification of the Chariot is in all the limbs),
for this matter of "nothing but One" is specifically in His heart.
And within the heart itself—in the innerness of the heart
[and as above, the explanation of "in your
heart" is within the heart],
for in the level of heart,
even in the heart of the Supernal Man,
since there is the matter of emotions there,
although He and His life
are truly one,
this is not the true essence of the matter of "nothing but One,"
and therefore they said "in your
heart,"
within your heart,
for in the point of the heart, the simple Oneness shines,
"nothing but One."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Based on this, the soul's state above is explained as being in the revelation of the point of the heart, where there is no "other" at all.

translations.translation: And based on this, we can explain that after the maamar says that the soul, when above, stood in its image before the Holy King, and
(furthermore)
was in ultimate attachment etc., it adds that it was in one will with Hashem alone, and there is no stranger with Him,
for the intention of "stranger"
(here)
is also for an existence that is nullified in the ultimate sense
(like the nullification of the letters of thought that are included in the intellect),
and this is what it says "and there is no stranger with Him,"
that the soul, when above,
was illuminated by the revelation of the point of the heart,
for from the perspective of this revelation, there is no stranger with Him,
"there is nothing but One in your heart."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The tribes, who are in BiY"A, also said "there is nothing but One in our heart," because the root of souls in Atzmus Ohr Ein Sof transcends all distinctions and is drawn equally to all levels.

translations.translation: 9) Now, based on the above, we must understand why the tribes said "there is nothing but One in our heart,"
for the tribes are in BiY"A
[as explained in many places
the distinction between the Patriarchs and the tribes,
that the Patriarchs are in Atzilus and the tribes are in BiY"A],
where the nullification in BiY"A is the nullification of Yichuda Tata'ah
(lower even than the nullification of the Chariot of Atzilus),
and nevertheless they said "there is nothing but One in our heart,"
for the matter of "nothing but One" is that there is no existence besides Him
(higher even than the Chariot of Atzilus).
And furthermore, they said "just as there is nothing but One in your heart, so there is nothing but One in our heart,"
that the matter of "nothing but One" in them and the matter of "nothing but One" in Yaakov,
both are equal.
And the Mitteler Rebbe explains in Shaarei Teshuvah there,
that the root of all the distinctions in the order of the chain of descent
[including the distinction between Yichuda Tata'ah of BiY"A and Yichuda Ila'ah of Atzilus,
and higher still, the nullification of "nothing but One"]
is in the Will for worlds,
which arose in His simple will to emanate and create,
and the root of the souls is in the very Atzmus of Ohr Ein Sof, above even the simple will
[in the "Who"
He consulted with the souls of the righteous],
and since, regarding the Atzmus of Ohr Ein Sof
(the root of souls)
all matters are equal,
therefore, the matter of "nothing but One" that is in Yaakov is drawn also into the tribes,
the souls of BiY"A.
